description:
Blue Sky Plan 5.0 is open with a Head/Neck CBCT scan loaded.

Your goal is to generate a synthetic Lateral Cephalogram (a standard 2D orthodontic X-ray projection) from this 3D volume.

Instructions:
1. Re-orient the 3D volume so the head is in a true lateral position (Sagittal view shows pure profile, Coronal view shows ear canals aligned).
2. Configure the Sagittal view to simulate an X-ray projection:
   - Increase the Slice Thickness to the maximum (or >120mm) to include the full skull width.
   - Set the rendering mode to 'Ray Sum', 'MIP', or 'X-Ray' (do not use 'Surface' or standard thin slice).
3. Adjust the Window/Level (Brightness/Contrast) so that BOTH the bony landmarks (skull base, jaws) AND the soft tissue profile (nose, lips, chin) are clearly visible.
4. Save the resulting Sagittal view as a high-resolution image named 'lateral_ceph.jpg' to 'C:\Users\Docker\Documents\BlueSkyPlan\'.

The final image must look like a traditional lateral cephalometric radiograph, not a 3D surface render or a thin slice.
